headline: The overnight chip story held and Dell's beat did not save it, while Europe leans on consumer names and the franc takes the haven bid before the 14:30 US data

findings.headline: Dell's record quarter fails to stop the chip unwind
findings.body: The counterpoint from last night did not hold: Dell turned lower in premarket trade, down about 7%, alongside Nvidia, Micron and AMD each off more than 5%. New reasons were added to the payback worry, with TrendForce forecasting NAND contract prices could start falling in early 2027 and the Wall Street Journal reporting wider credit spreads and dearer default insurance on tech debt. That shifts the debate from AI demand to the financing of AI capex, which is harder for one strong earnings print to answer.

findings.headline: Europe holds up on a consumer rotation as a new US tariff round looms
findings.body: Europe is leaning on consumer and luxury names rather than tech: Remy Cointreau jumped about 10% on new targets through 2031/32, lifting Swatch and Richemont, while Prosus fell on a profit miss. The risk not yet in prices is the US Trade Representative's excess-capacity findings on 16 trading partners including the EU and China, which reports say would stack new duties on existing tariffs. Germany's Q3 GDP was also revised down to 0.1% with exports down 1%, so exporters have little cushion if those duties land.

findings.headline: The franc is the haven of choice into PCE
findings.body: The euro has fallen to its weakest against the franc since early June, with the franc, dollar and yen the strongest G10 currencies as Asia's sell-off revived risk aversion. Markets price about a 96% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike on 8-9 December, and economists expect headline PCE at 3.8% from 3.6%, so a hot print at 14:30 Zurich would hit growth stocks that are already lagging. The SNB has said it is ready to act in the currency market if needed, which caps how far the franc rally can run without a response.

view: Our view: The overnight story held, and the market is now questioning how AI capex is financed, not just whether demand is there, which is why a beat like Dell's did not help. Europe's consumer-led resilience is real but exposed to the tariff findings, and a hot PCE this afternoon would turn rotation into wider de-risking.
